findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows spatial routing of underground electric lines, transformer pads, pull boxes, and meters. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed: NO load calculations or capacity analysis visible anywhere on the sheet. No tables, schedules, or numerical load data present. Engineer's Summary Letter (05-utilities.md) covers only water and wastewater utilities, not electrical. No supplementary document containing load calculations identified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires 'electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis' be provided to AE Design. The preliminary nature of Sheet 21's design (no service specifications, no voltage/phase/amperage shown) indicates load analysis has not been performed or submitted. For a 39-unit development with 8 buildings, electrical demand calculations are fundamental to determining service requirements. The absence of this documentation is a clear deficiency.
findings.comment: Electrical load calculations and demand projections not provided to Austin Energy. Sheet 21 shows preliminary layout only without load analysis, demand calculations, or capacity specifications. Submit detailed electrical load calculations for all 39 units and buildings, including peak demand, connected load, demand factors per NEC standards, and capacity analysis to support service requirements determination.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) vision analysis found: NO voltage specifications visible, NO phase requirements labeled, NO service capacity/amperage shown. The sheet shows proposed transformer pad and pull box locations with labels ('Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Underground Electric Line') but no technical parameters. No service characteristics specified anywhere on the sheet or in supplementary documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires voltage and service size specifications necessary for service be provided to AE Design. These are critical parameters that must be determined by Austin Energy Design based on customer load requirements. The absence of voltage (e.g., 120/240V, 480V), phase (single-phase, 3-phase), and service amperage on the drawings indicates Austin Energy has not yet provided these determinations. Sheet 21's preliminary status and lack of specifications confirm this deficiency.
findings.comment: Voltage and service size specifications not provided. Sheet 21 shows preliminary layout without service voltage, phase requirements, or amperage specifications. Submit Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming available service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity in amps) for this site, or indicate which specifications will be determined during detailed design phase per AE direction.

findings.observation: Master Comment Report (02-electric-review.md) references AE site comments on a Bluebeam link (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw) but this link is inaccessible to reviewer. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary design for all sites requiring AE Design coordination. This project clearly requires AE Design review (new service to 39 units, transmission line crossing property). While the Master Comment Report acknowledges that AE has reviewed comments (available on Bluebeam), the formal approval correspondence itself is not available in the submitted documentation. The preliminary designation of Sheet 21 and absence of AE approval signature/stamp indicates formal approval has not been provided in documentable form.
findings.comment: Proof of correspondence from Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electrical design not submitted. While AE comments are referenced in master report, no signed approval letter or correspondence confirming preliminary design review and approval by Austin Energy Design is present in submitted documents. Submit email or letter from Austin Energy Design (Rosemary Avila or assigned designer) confirming review and approval of the preliminary electrical design plan.

findings.observation: No service verification letter from Austin Energy confirming that utility service can be provided to the site is present in supplementary documents. The Engineer's Summary Letter (05-utilities.md) documents only water and wastewater service verification from Austin Water ('Suitable and Sufficient Existing Service' letters referenced on Sheet 3), but contains no reference to electric service verification. No letter from Austin Energy identifying necessary easements or service upgrades for the 39-unit development was found.
findings.reasoning: Reviewer convention requires a letter from Austin Energy stating utility service can be provided and identifying necessary easements or upgrades. For a site with transmission easement crossing and new service to 39 units, Austin Energy must confirm service availability and identify any service upgrade requirements. The absence of this letter is a deficiency. Sheet 3 shows transmission line coordination requirements, suggesting transmission engineering involvement, but no formal service availability confirmation letter is on file.
findings.comment: Letter from Austin Energy confirming service availability not submitted. Austin Energy must provide letter confirming that electric service can be provided to the site, identifying the service characteristics available at the proposed point of service, and detailing any necessary easements, line extensions, or infrastructure upgrades required to serve the 39-unit development.

findings.comment: Agent Authorization Letter specific to Austin Energy review or Owner Authorization Letter explicitly naming 'Austin Energy' not provided. findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 contains detailed Electric Transmission Notes confirming transmission line crosses property with specific requirements (25-foot clearance from structures, pre-construction safety meeting, no digging/grading, 46,000 lb tandem axle road loading for easement access). Andrew Perez contact provided for transmission coordination (512-505-7153). This confirms transmission line involvement. However, whether CAD files have been submitted separately to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for specialized review is not confirmed in the submitted documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires CAD files be submitted for AE Transmission Engineering review when project involves transmission lines (≥60kV). Sheet 3 Block 20 confirms transmission line is present and requires engineering review. While preliminary design exists on Sheet 21, whether the formal CAD submission package has been delivered to Austin Energy's Transmission Engineering department specifically is not documented in the available pre-processed materials. The Master Comment Report's Bluebeam link might contain this information but is inaccessible.
findings.comment: CAD files submission to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering not confirmed. While transmission line involvement is documented on Sheet 3 with specific engineering requirements, no confirmation that CAD files have been submitted to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for specialized transmission review is present in supplementary documents. Submit transmittal email or receipt confirming CAD files were provided to AE Transmission Engineering group for transmission crossing analysis.

findings.observation: Site plan sheets are provided as processed documents. No metadata regarding AutoCAD file version (2016 or newer) is available from the pre-processed documentation. Sheet 21 and other sheets show professional design layout but version information of the source CAD files is not accessible.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires AutoCAD files submitted for transmission or land development review be version 2016 or newer. Since transmission line involvement is confirmed (Sheet 3 Block 20), AutoCAD submissions are required. However, the version of CAD files used cannot be verified from the available documentation. This is an accessibility issue with the pre-processed materials rather than a definitive pass/fail determination.
findings.comment: AutoCAD file version not verifiable. While site plan drawings are provided, the version of AutoCAD files submitted to Austin Energy cannot be confirmed from available documentation. Verify and document that all CAD files submitted to Austin Energy (Design and Transmission Engineering) are AutoCAD 2016 or newer format. Provide submission confirmation or file properties documentation showing version.

findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 confirms transmission line crosses property and provides detailed transmission requirements. However, Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) does NOT show plan and profile views of the transmission line relationship to proposed infrastructure. The transmission line is mentioned in notes on Sheet 3 but is not graphically depicted with clearances and spatial relationships in detail on electrical drawings. No separate transmission design drawing submitted.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires AutoCAD drawings be submitted to Austin Energy transmission reviewer 'when project involves transmission lines' and specifically requires 'plan and profile views' showing how proposed infrastructure relates to transmission facilities. While Sheet 3 documents transmission presence and requirements, the electrical design drawings (Sheet 21) do not show transmission line with plan/profile views demonstrating safe clearances and separation. The preliminary status of Sheet 21 and absence of transmission line graphic representation on electrical plans is a deficiency.
findings.comment: AutoCAD drawings showing transmission line plan and profile views not provided. Transmission engineering analysis requires plan and profile drawings depicting the transmission line and proposed site infrastructure (buildings, drainage, utilities) with clearances and separation demonstrated in plan and elevation. Prepare and submit detailed plan and profile drawings showing transmission line, proposed buildings, and all infrastructure in AutoCAD format, with clearances labeled per National Electric Safety Code (NESC) standards.

findings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 documents transmission line presence with clearance requirements but does NOT show any proposed infrastructure crossing underneath the transmission line in detail. Sheet 21 (electrical design) shows underground utility routing but transmission line crossing profile design is not explicitly shown. The facts about the transmission easement (25-foot clearance from structures, vehicle load requirements for roads in easement) are documented but no specific crossing detail in AutoCAD profile view is present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires 'profile design of crossing infrastructure' in AutoCAD drawings when proposed infrastructure crosses AE transmission line. The transmission easement presence is confirmed (Sheet 3), but whether site drainage, utility lines, or buildings cross the transmission line spatially is not clearly depicted in profile view on the electrical drawings. If any site infrastructure (stormwater, utilities, buildings) crosses the transmission path, profile design detail is required. This may not be applicable if infrastructure avoids transmission crossing, but this must be explicitly confirmed.
findings.comment: Profile design for transmission line crossing not clearly documented. If proposed site infrastructure (drainage, utilities, buildings) crosses the transmission easement path, AutoCAD profile drawings must show the crossing design with clearances and separation per NESC standards. Confirm which site elements interact with transmission line and provide profile drawings for any crossings, or confirm avoidance of transmission line crossing entirely.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design with proposed transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground routing. However, no separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan is submitted showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views independent from the site plan. The electrical design is shown on Sheet 21 integrated with the general site plan, not as a standalone AE distribution plan document. No callouts reference an AE Distribution Plan for detailed design with underground routing specifications, cable depths, or clearance details.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Austin Energy Distribution Plan not submitted separate from site plan showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views when modifications to existing AE facilities are proposed.' The transmission easement and service extension to 8 buildings constitute AE facility modifications requiring detailed design. The preliminary status of Sheet 21 and integration with site plan (rather than as a standalone AE distribution design document) indicates this requirement may not be satisfied. A separate, detailed distribution plan with profile views showing cable depths, duct banks, transformer specifications, and service feeds is needed.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Distribution Plan showing detailed design not submitted separately from site plan. Submit detailed Austin Energy Distribution Plan as a separate document showing plan and profile views of all electric service infrastructure, including proposed underground cable routing with depths, duct specifications, transformer pad details, service feeds to each building, clearances from other utilities, and cable size/type specifications per Austin Energy standards.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric routing near drainage features (biofiltration/detention pond is prominent site feature per facts and Sheet 15/16). However, no profile plans are provided showing electrical utilities with vertical clearances from drainage features. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 found only plan view; no profile sheets showing electrical cable depth clearances from pond bottom, crest, or outlet structures. Sheets 15-16 show pond design but do not include electrical utility profiles demonstrating required clearances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.7 establish clearance requirements from drainage features. UCM § 1.16.0(1)(iv) requires profile plans showing electrical facilities when they interact with drainage. The site has a prominent biofiltration/detention pond with electric service routing nearby. To demonstrate compliance with vertical clearance requirements (particularly if underground services pass beneath or adjacent to pond), profile views are required. The absence of profile plans showing electrical utilities relative to drainage features is a deficiency.
findings.comment: Profile plans showing electrical facilities with required clearances from drainage features not provided. Submit profile drawings showing underground electric cable routing relative to the biofiltration/detention pond (including pond bottom elevation, crest, outlet structure) demonstrating minimum clearances per UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.7. Include cable depth, duct specifications, and setback from pond structures.

findings.observation: No correspondence from Austin Energy indicating whether line extension is required or whether service can be provided via existing infrastructure is present in supplementary documents. Master Comment Report Electric Review section references AE site comments on Bluebeam (inaccessible) but contains no summary of line extension determination. No cost responsibility acknowledgment from developer regarding line extension fees is visible. Facts.md notes existing 5-foot electric easements on property suggesting some AE infrastructure may already be present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.12 requires developer financial responsibility acknowledgment for line extension when required. The determination of whether line extension is necessary requires Austin Energy Design evaluation based on existing infrastructure capacity and location relative to proposed service point. Without correspondence from AE Design confirming line extension necessity (or confirming service can be provided from existing infrastructure), this item cannot be definitively evaluated. The Bluebeam comments may address this but are inaccessible.
findings.comment: Developer financial responsibility for line extension not confirmed. Austin Energy must determine whether line extension is required to serve the proposed 39-unit development and provide written determination. If line extension is required, developer must acknowledge financial responsibility in writing. Submit Austin Energy correspondence confirming line extension requirement (or service-only status) and developer's signed acknowledgment of cost responsibility if applicable.

findings.observation: No Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee or receipt is present in supplementary documents. Master Comment Report and completeness check results do not reference fee payment or waiver. Engineer's Summary Letter, authorization documents, and financial documentation in supplementary files do not include AE site plan review fee payment evidence.
findings.reasoning: Reviewer convention requires submission of Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee as a prerequisite to land development review. While Austin Energy completeness check is marked 'complete,' evidence of fee payment (receipt, invoice, or waiver) is not available in the submitted documentation. This could indicate the fee has not been submitted or was not included in the pre-processed documentation package.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee not provided. Submit payment receipt, invoice, or waiver documentation confirming that the Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee required for land development coordination has been paid or appropriately waived.

findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) is the original 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat, which is historical background. Vision analysis found NO plat notes on this sheet mentioning Austin Energy requirements. The sheet shows historical approval stamps and dedication language but contains NO eight required plat notes specified in UCM § 1.16.0(8): (i) Austin Energy pruning/removal rights, (ii) easement and access provision, (iii) owner erosion control and tree protection responsibilities, (iv) clearance maintenance responsibility, (v-viii) transmission easement restrictions. No current project plat with AE notes was found in the supplementary documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires eight specific plat notes when site has electric facilities and easements. This project has transmission easement (Sheet 3 Block 20), electric distribution easements (facts.md), and new service design. The required plat notes are not present on the plat documents provided. Either the current project plat has not been prepared yet, or the required AE notes have not been added. This is a clear deficiency.
findings.comment: Required plat notes for electric utilities and transmission easement not included. Prepare project plat (if not already prepared) or update existing plat to include all eight required notes per UCM § 1.16.0(8): (i) Austin Energy pruning/removal rights within easements, (ii) easement and access provision for AE, (iii) owner responsibility for erosion control and tree protection, (iv) owner responsibility for clearance maintenance around AE facilities, and (v-viii) specific transmission easement restrictions per UCM § 1.16.0(8)(v-viii) including prohibition of structures, landscaping, and fencing within easement.

applicableAreas: Electric facility clearances on site plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground routing with location labels but NO clearance dimensions are shown. Vision analysis confirmed absence of clearance callouts, setback dimensions from buildings, property lines, drainage features, or other infrastructure. The transmission line requirements on Sheet 3 Block 20 specify clearances (25 feet from structures, 20 feet for aerial equipment/staging) but these are notes, not dimensioned on electrical drawings. No clearance schedule or detailed specification table accompanies the electrical design.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires plans demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities per design and safety standards. The preliminary designation of Sheet 21 and complete absence of dimensioned clearances (setbacks, vertical clearances from pond, horizontal separations) fails to meet this requirement. While transmission clearance requirements are listed in notes, the actual proposed site layout does not include clearance dimensions to verify compliance.
findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate sufficient clearances for electric facilities. Sheet 21 lacks dimensioned clearance information for proposed electric infrastructure. Add clearance dimensions to electrical plans showing: (1) minimum setbacks of transformer pads and pull boxes from buildings per NEC standards, (2) clearances from all drainage features per UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.7, (3) clearances from other utilities, (4) 25-foot clearance from transmission structures, and (5) clearance maintenance areas accessible for Austin Energy.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed electric infrastructure (transformer pads, pull boxes, underground routing) but does not show electric utility easement areas or boundaries dimensioned on the plans. Facts.md indicates two recorded electric easements (5-foot each) from the 1975 plat (Vol 73/76, C8S-75-160), but their current location relative to proposed improvements is not confirmed on the site plan. Transmission easement requirements are documented (Sheet 3 Block 20) but easement boundary is not dimensioned or metes-and-bounds described on the electrical drawings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(3) requires plans demonstrate sufficient electric utilities easements or provide metes and bounds descriptions for additional easements required by Austin Energy. Sheet 21 does not show existing electric easement locations/dimensions. Given the transmission line crossing and new service points to 8 buildings, additional easements will be required. The absence of dimensioned easement areas and metes-and-bounds descriptions for required easements is a deficiency.
findings.comment: Electric utilities easements not dimensioned and metes and bounds descriptions not provided. Add dimensioned easement areas to site plan showing: (1) existing 5-foot electric easements from 1975 plat and their relationship to proposed improvements, (2) transmission easement boundaries with dimensions, and (3) any additional easements required for service feeds to buildings. For new easements required by Austin Energy, provide complete metes and bounds legal descriptions with bearings, distances, and reference points per survey control.

applicableAreas: Austin Energy facility access and maintenance
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed site development with buildings, utilities, and infrastructure but does not explicitly depict access routes for Austin Energy personnel and equipment to reach electric facilities (transformer pads, pull boxes, underground service feeds). The transmission easement requirements (Sheet 3 Block 20) specify '24-hour access to electric facilities shall be maintained' and 'roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle' but these are noted requirements, not shown graphically on the electrical design.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(4) requires plans demonstrate that development will maintain Austin Energy personnel ability to access and maintain current and proposed electric facilities. Sheet 21 does not show explicitly marked access routes, turning radiuses for AE vehicles, or equipment staging areas for transformer/cable maintenance. The preliminary nature and lack of access planning indicates this requirement is not met.
findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate access for Austin Energy personnel to maintain electric facilities. Add to electrical and site plans: (1) clearly marked access routes and truck turning areas for Austin Energy vehicles to reach all transformer pads and underground service locations, (2) equipment staging areas for maintenance vehicles, (3) confirmation that roads within transmission easement comply with 46,000 lb tandem axle loading requirement, and (4) verification that no permanent structures, landscaping, or fencing will obstruct AE facility access.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) vision analysis found: NO service voltage shown, NO phase designation (single-phase or 3-phase), NO service capacity/amperage specified. The sheet shows infrastructure locations but no electrical parameters. No corresponding Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming available service characteristics for this location is present in supplementary documents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.2 establishes that Austin Energy Design holds exclusive determination authority for service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity). Plans cannot show self-determined service specifications; they must be confirmed by AE Design based on site evaluation and customer needs. Sheet 21 lacks these determinations entirely, and no AE Design approval letter providing the determinations is available. This is a deficiency both in the plan documentation and in the coordination process.
findings.comment: Plans show preliminary electrical design without Austin Energy Design approval of service characteristics. Provide Austin Energy Design approval letter confirming the service characteristics available and approved for this site, specifying: (1) service voltage available (e.g., 120/240V, 480V), (2) phase configuration (single-phase or 3-phase), and (3) service capacity in amps. Do not show service specifications on plans until AE Design provides written determination.

applicableAreas: Affordable housing line extension fee waiver (if applicable)
findings.observation: Facts.md shows project is 39 'multi-family townhome units' (new development). Development specifications note 'Proposed Use: 39 multi-family townhome units.' No documentation from Housing and Planning Department confirming S.M.A.R.T. Housing Program participation is present. The consolidated site plan application (03-property-attributes.md) does not reference affordable housing status or S.M.A.R.T. Housing participation. If any affordable housing waiver is being claimed, supporting documentation is absent.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.12 specifies that affordable housing line extension fee waivers (for projects with ≥75% affordable units) require documentation from Housing and Planning Department demonstrating S.M.A.R.T. Housing Program compliance. If this project includes affordable units and is claiming a waiver, the documentation is missing. If the project is NOT affordable housing, this item would not apply. However, the absence of any designation suggests this may not be applicable, but the applicant should explicitly confirm affordable housing status and any related fee waiver claims.
findings.comment: If affordable housing line extension fee waiver is claimed, Housing and Planning Department documentation not provided. If the project includes any portion of affordable residential units and a line extension fee waiver is claimed, submit: (1) Housing and Planning Department determination confirming S.M.A.R.T. Housing Program compliance, (2) certification of percentage of affordable units (≥75% required for full waiver), and (3) calculation of waived fees. If no affordable housing status applies, explicitly state 'No affordable housing' on application.
